gloss: to worry needlessly in advance; to borrow trouble

definitions.gloss: to worry needlessly in advance; to borrow trouble
definitions.explanation: To worry about something before it happens, especially when the worry turns out to be unnecessary. Almost always appears in the set expression 取り越し苦労.

examples.japanese: {取|と}り{越|こ}し{苦労|くろう}だったね。
examples.english: It was needless worry, wasn't it?

examples.japanese: {試験|しけん}の{結果|けっか}は{取|と}り{越|こ}し{苦労|くろう}で、ちゃんと{合格|ごうかく}していた。
examples.english: My worries about the exam results were needless — I passed just fine.

examples.japanese: まだ{何|なに}も{決|き}まっていないのに、{先|さき}のことを{取|と}り{越|こ}して{心配|しんぱい}するのはやめよう。
examples.english: Nothing has been decided yet, so let's stop worrying about the future prematurely.

notes:
This verb is most commonly encountered in the compound noun {取|と}り{越|こ}し{苦労|くろう} (needless worry; borrowing trouble), which is a very common expression. The standalone verb form is less frequent.

KEY EXPRESSION:
- {取|と}り{越|こ}し{苦労|くろう}: needless anxiety; worrying about things that haven't happened yet

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {取|と}り{越|こ}し{苦労|くろう}だった: it was needless worry
- {取|と}り{越|こ}し{苦労|くろう}をする: to worry needlessly
- {取|と}り{越|こ}して{心配|しんぱい}する: to worry prematurely
Godan verb (す row). Conjugates: {取|と}り{越|こ}さない, {取|と}り{越|こ}して, {取|と}り{越|こ}します.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {杞憂|きゆう}: groundless fears — more literary, from a Chinese story
- {心配|しんぱい}し{過|す}ぎ: worrying too much — more general
